 Search The Site Massachusetts Just Took a Major Step Toward Ending Changing the Clocks Forever Massachusetts Just Took a Major Step Toward Ending Changing the Clocks Forever
 Barry Richard Barry Richard Published: November 3, 2026 Getty Images Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 How are you coping with the 4:30 p.m. sunset and driving home in the dark after work? What happened to watching the sun sink slowly into the ocean while strolling at Horseneck Beach after dinner? Life seemed much more civilized back then, before we fell back to Eastern Standard Time. 
 For those of you jonesing for a little more light at the end of the day, Daylight Saving Time returns on March 14, 2027. That's a whole winter away.
 Congress has been talking about eliminating the biannual time change, but getting Congress to agree on anything is always challenging. Don't hold your breath waiting.
 Barry Richard/Townsquare Media Massachusetts May Be On The Road To Dumping Biannual Clock Change Fighting the 4:30 P.M. Sunset
 Massachusetts, however, has taken the first step toward leaving the clocks alone all year with the Senate Rules Committee's passage of An Act Relative to Massachusetts Time Zones and Sunshine Protection (S 2157) . The bill would move Massachusetts to  Atlantic Standard Time year-round, which is an hour ahead of the Eastern Time Zone.
 But there's a catch.
 Inside Bill S 2157 and the Regional Catch
 "The move would only take effect if at least two neighboring states agree to join in a permanent move," reported the  Boston Herald's Tim Dunn.
 Ella Adams/State House News Service Massachusetts May Be On The Road To Dumping Biannual Clock Change State House News Service  reported the five Democrats on the Senate Rules Committee voted to advance the legislation; however, "The Committee's two Republicans did not take a for-or-against position."
 "The Senate voted to advance the bill during its informal session Thursday, although a second vote would be needed to send it to the House," according to SHNS.
 Get our free mobile app Mass. Senate Support for Permanent Time
 Senate President Karen Spilka said last March, "This should be the last time that Massachusetts has to change our clocks. It would be better for our health, safer for our roads, and remove one more complication from everyone's lives."
